chunks: In their wealth is the right of the suppliant and the deprived.

key_terms.أَمْوَالِهِمْ: Their wealth (plural of mal, referring to possessions and assets)
key_terms.السَّائِلِ: The suppliant (one who asks for charity)
key_terms.وَالْمَحْرُومِ: And the deprived (one who is in need but may not ask)

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'suppliant' and 'deprived' mentioned in the Quran as having a right to the wealth of believers?
ai.summary: This verse, central to Shia jurisprudence, distinguishes between the *sā'il* (one who asks) and the *maḥrūm* (the deprived who do not ask), emphasizing proactive charity. It serves as a foundational text for the concept of *zakāt* and *khums*, linking material wealth to spiritual purification and social justice. The inclusion of the *maḥrūm* underscores the duty to identify and support the needy even when they remain silent, reflecting a holistic approach to communal welfare.
